subject: HeliOSCare - post-demo budget slab + concurrency walkthrough
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@helioscare.com>; procurement@helioscare.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HeliOSCare - post-demo budget slab + concurrency walkthrough

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning, Samira — great conversation. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get a clean Hosted API pricing proposal over to procurement.

Summary of what we saw / what HeliOSCare needs:
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant (patient intake + symptom triage + simple clinical summarization).
- Estimated monthly tokens (ballpark from your product team): ~40M - 60M tokens/month.
- Peak shape: short morning spike 07:30–09:30 PST and occasional post-release surges. Observed peak concurrent TPS estimate from your ops note: ~70–90 TPS for 3–5 minute windows.
- Latency SLO: 250–350ms p50 for short requests (<=512 tokens) — mentioned as important for UI responsiveness.

Clarifying questions we need answered to finalize pricing slab and canary plan:
1) Are those 40–60M tokens inclusive of embeddings (search) traffic or is that strictly generation? If embeddings are separate, can you share monthly embedding units?
2) What percent of requests will be <=512 tokens vs >512 tokens (rough split)? Even rough split (e.g., 80/20) helps with per-token costing assumptions.
3) Any regulatory constraints that push you to Private rather than Hosted? (You answered no in the call but wanted to confirm.)

Target pricing range we discussed on the call: goal is to hit an effective $/1M tokens in the mid-teens to low-20s depending on burst needs and committed slab. For a first pass we will prepare two options:
- 50M monthly commitment slab (tiered unit price) with burstable concurrency up to 120 TPS and canary rollout plan.
- Lower commitment 20M slab + on-demand bursts (higher unit price but lower commitment).

Next immediate steps:
- Samira / procurement: confirm whether embeddings are in scope and share any embedding monthly estimate. Also send PO timeline if available.
- Redwood (Vanessa + Karthik): send a draft hosted pricing quote + canary ops plan and suggested instance/model for the canary. I will assemble usage assumptions into the attached spreadsheet.

Attachments: HeliosCare_usage_preview.xlsx (contains our working token-profile assumptions).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15m follow-up if that’s easiest.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
From: Samira Khan <samira@helioscare.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helioscare.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 12:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: HeliOSCare - post-demo budget slab + concurrency walkthrough

Thanks Logan — good recap. A few answers below and one follow-up: 

Answers:
- The 40–60M is our current product-level estimate for generation only (the triage replies and summaries). Embeddings for search are separate and currently very small — ~1M embedding units/month (we expect to keep that low for now).
- Token length split: roughly 85% of calls are short (<=512 tokens) and ~15% are longer (512-2k) when a clinician requests extended summaries.
- Regulatory: Hosted is fine for now; we’ll revisit Private later if telemetry/audit needs grow.

Budget target: Our CFO prefers a target of $15–$20 per 1M tokens (they mentioned $18 as a comfortable midpoint) but will want to see how peak TPS affects the effective unit price.

Procurement timeline: We can have a draft PO within 2 weeks, but we need a quote and SLA language to attach.

One ask: can Redwood propose a short canary plan showing how we would protect against degraded latency during the 07:30–09:30 spike? We’re especially sensitive to p95 latency.

Happy to review your spreadsheet; I’ll loop in our infra lead separately if you need more telemetry.

— Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Product | HeliOSCare
samira@helioscare.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@helioscare.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@helioscare.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HeliOSCare - post-demo budget slab + concurrency walkthrough

Appreciate the quick answers, Samira — that helps a lot. We’ll put together two formal quote options that map to the ranges you outlined and include an explicit modeled effective $/1M tokens across your expected weekly profile (morning spike + steady-state).

On the canary/latency protection: Vanessa and Karthik will include an ops playbook that uses:
- pre-warming + short-lived burst capacity during 07:00–09:30 PST windows,
- a prioritized routing policy so on-UI traffic hits lower-latency instances (dedicated pool for interactive calls), and
- automatic fallbacks to a smaller model variant for non-critical background requests (e.g., bulk summarization).

We’ll attach SLA p50/p95 numbers and a proposed trial SLA for the first 30 days. Expect a draft quote + canary playbook by EOD Friday. If procurement can share any preferred SLA language, we’ll incorporate it.

— Logan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@helioscare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@helioscare.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HeliOSCare - post-demo budget slab + concurrency walkthrough

Looping in some technical specifics for the quote and canary plan — copying the team’s recommended assumptions that will drive unit economics: 

Assumptions we’ll price off: 
- Baseline model: trimmed-llama-3-13b (quantized) for the interactive path; fallback small model for background summarization.
- Effective tokenization: use a conservative 1.15x multiplier on raw token counts to account for system tokens + function-calls.
- Modeled monthly volume scenarios: Low: 25M gen tokens; Mid: 50M gen tokens; High: 75M gen tokens.
- Peak design: 120 TPS headroom for 15-minute windows to cover burst risk (matches your 70–90 TPS observed).

Pricing sketch we’ll present (examples not final):
- Mid slab (50M/mo): $18 per 1M gen tokens (hosted) with a guaranteed burst allowance and SLA p95 target of 750ms.
- Lower slab (25M/mo): $24 per 1M gen tokens with burst on demand.

We’ll include a modeled cost table in the spreadsheet showing per-request effective cost at your 85/15 split and at the morning spike. Also including a short runbook for autoscaling triggers and a canary checklist for the first 48 hours post-rollout.

If that pricing sketch is directionally reasonable, I’ll convert to a formal line-item quote and attach Redwood-hosted-pricing-quote-v1.pdf.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
